title: dev/ function-signature check is Linux-only; skip its tests on Windows instead of adding Windows path handling
answers: Why does the function signature test skip on Windows?
How do I handle Windows paths in dev/check_function_signatures.py?
Should I add Windows path support to the function signature checker?
Why is test_check_function_signatures skipped on win32?
body:
Convention: the function-signature compatibility check runs only in the Ubuntu lint job, so its test module is skipped on Windows via a module-level pytestmark skipif on sys.platform == "win32".
Where: tests/dev/test_check_function_signatures.py:pytestmark gates the whole module; dev/check_function_signatures.py:check_signature_compatibility is left unchanged.
Fix pattern: when a dev/ lint script's tests fail on Windows, skip the module with a reason string rather than adding Windows-specific path logic (e.g. normalizing git object specs or WindowsPath handling) to the script.
Constraints: this was a CI-driven choice. It applies only while the script is not executed on Windows runners. If the check is ever wired into a Windows job, the skip must be removed and Windows path behavior (such as forward-slash git object specs like HEAD^1:mlflow/foo.py) needs real coverage.
applies: Applies to dev/check_function_signatures.py and its tests under tests/dev/; not to product code under mlflow/.
says: Function signature compatibility verification tests are skipped on Windows development machines.
Why does the API signature compatibility check not run on Windows?
Enable API signature verification on Windows instead of skipping the test suite.

When dev/ lint script tests fail on Windows, developers must skip the test module with a reason string instead of introducing Windows-specific path normalization or WindowsPath handling. This rule applies strictly to dev/check_function_signatures.py and tests/dev/ tests rather than product code under mlflow/. If the check is ever executed on Windows runners, the skip must be removed to provide real coverage for forward-slash git object specs.
